HTX's numbered addresses ('HTX 8', 'HTX 34', 'HTX 80', ...) don't follow OKX/Bybit's 'Hot Wallet N' convention -- individually checked several: all either Etherscan-tagged 'Deposit Address' or currently near-zero balance with no transactions in 180+ days (drained/rotated out, not a live main wallet). No genuine large-balance, currently-active HTX address surfaced via web search in this pass. Needs a different research method (e.g. checking USDT/USDC top-holder lists for an HTX-tagged entry) than what worked for OKX/Bybit -- deferred, not fabricated.

known_false_positive_traps: Substring-matching 'binance' (or any exchange name) against a label/nameTag field catches OTHER platforms' individual deposit wallets INTO that exchange (e.g. 'Bilaxy: Binance Dep: 0x...', 'Alameda Research: Binance Deposit') -- these are not the exchange's own wallets. This is how the eth-labels dataset's 5102 'binance' matches were almost entirely false positives. Always verify against the exchange's own primary label page, not a substring match.
'0x: Coinbase Wallet Proxy' is a 0x-protocol smart contract, unrelated to Coinbase the company -- a naming coincidence, not a Coinbase wallet.

A search result's stated wallet balance can be badly stale (Kraken 3 was quoted at 801,052 ETH in one search snippet; the live Etherscan value was 0.057 ETH). Balances are not durable facts -- only addresses/labels are worth recording here; always fetch balances live at run time.

A wallet's own dedicated Etherscan label page (/accounts/label/<name>) is not always the right list for a given exchange -- Kraken's page returns per-user deposit addresses, not the main custody wallets, which had to be found via general search instead.

An address literally named 'Exchange: Hot Wallet N' is not guaranteed to be a main custody wallet -- OKX's own 'Hot Wallet' and 'Hot Wallet 2' are Etherscan-tagged 'Deposit Address' with near-zero balance despite the name; always check the live balance AND Etherscan's own secondary tag ('Deposit Address' vs plain 'Exchange'), not just the label text.

In this session, etherscan.io's /accounts/label/<slug> listing pages were Cloudflare-gated ('Just a moment...', never resolved after repeated waits/retries) while individual /address/<addr> pages loaded normally -- when the label-listing approach that worked in an earlier session stops working, fall back to web search for candidate addresses and verify each individually, don't conclude the exchange has no findable wallets.
